title: UK Bans Disposable BBQs Because They're Starting Wildfires
summary:
Have you ever used a disposable barbecue? It's a small grill you can use once and throw away. But in the UK right now, you can't buy one. The government has banned selling them for a while because they're causing wildfires.

The UK is having a very hot, dry summer. That makes the ground and plants super dry, like a tinderbox—something that catches fire very easily. Disposable barbecues have started many serious wildfires across the country. So the government said stores can't sell them in England, Scotland, or Wales.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, "Britain is a tinderbox right now. Setting a fire in any outdoor setting of any kind is a risk to other people's homes, it's a risk to other people's lives, don't do it, please don't do it."

This year, there have been 1,017 wildfires in England and Wales, matching last year's record. Firefighters are working hard to put out many blazes, especially in the West Midlands. Burnham said he wants to get special firefighting planes, like the ones used in Europe and the US, to help.

Some stores had already stopped selling disposable barbecues because of an agreement made in 2023. But now the government is making it a rule for everyone. Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said it's a "common-sense step to protect lives and the environment."

So if you're in the UK this summer, remember: no open fires, be careful with cigarettes, and definitely no disposable BBQs. The country is just too dry and dangerous right now.
why_it_matters: This shows how one small item can create big danger when the weather changes, and why rules may suddenly change to keep families and homes safe.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham (the UK leader in this story) and Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds (a government official in charge of business and trade) supported the ban.
During heatwaves, many countries limit outdoor fires, grills, and cigarettes because dry grass can catch fire very quickly.
